result:
The slowdown reproduces on today's master. The cause is not the guest CPU: the renderer thread twice a frame stops recording and waits for the GPU to finish before it can continue. I haven't named a lever yet. The one measurement that would name it is dropped by the dispatcher's logcat filter, and I've filed a board request to fix that. PR #374 is ready and the finding is posted on #372.

**Reproduction.** Two full runs on master both averaged 13.8 fps over the demo window (time-weighted), against 14.9 on the issue's build. A diagnostic (perflog) build read 13.3.

**Where a demo frame goes** (perflog build, median ms per guest frame):

| | demo | menus |
|---|---|---|
| guest frame | 68.1 | 17.3 |
| renderer waiting for the GPU to finish | **32.1** | 0.2 |
| recording ~2,000–3,000 draws | 23.0 | 3.1 |
| renderer idle | 2.5 | 13.2 |
| GPU busy | 37.1 | 0.2 |

The wait comes from two surface-download finishes per frame in the demo; the menus have none. They force recording and GPU work to run one after the other instead of overlapping.

**Falsifier ("guest-CPU bound"): broken on every run, but not by your 60% threshold.** The guest CPU thread is 92–95% busy in the demo, but also 78–97% in the 60 fps menus, because the guest spins. That share can't tell the two cases apart and never drops below 60%. What does tell them apart:
- The renderer is 96–98% busy, idle only ~2 ms per frame.
- Commands waiting for the renderer grow from ~4.6 KB to ~94 KB, so the guest is ahead of it.
- Flip wait is 0.

TLB and translation costs are about 1% (not #68's territory here).

**Lever.** There are seven places that can trigger a surface download, and a counter in the perflog build says which one fires. The dispatcher's logcat filter (`dispatcher.sh:1356`) drops that line, and it also drops `hakuX-pace` from every dispatched soak. So your "record the `hakuX-pace` line" wasn't possible either. The board request asks to add `hakuX-pace:I hakuX-stall:I xemu-gpu:I`. After that, one perflog soak names the site. Removing both waits would reach roughly 27 fps at most, after which the GPU's 37 ms becomes the limit. No prediction is registered because no source change is named.

**Not done or incomplete:**
- No simpleperf top-20 and no loadsample thread split. Both scripts call `adb` directly, which lanes can't do. I used the always-on counters and the perflog phase lines instead.
- The Thor run on master that died at 125 s only gave ~10 s of demo, so I queued a replacement to get two full runs.
- 3 of 5 Thor soaks today lost the guest early with no crash line; the Nova shows the same on other titles. It's not Blinx and I didn't investigate it.

Raw logs for all six runs are in `/home/justin/hakux-work/perf/2026-09-26/blinx372/`. The write-up is `docs/investigations/perf-blinx-372.md`; `docs/lanes/blinx372/NOTES.md` has a "do not repeat" list and the exact next request.
